stage.title: Stage
stage.description: What the object shows and lets the learner do: the clock face, two gears, teeth that light up as they pass, one very large gear, the last gear to size, the last gear to roll back to the centre, or the dial seen through.

bigTeeth.title: Teeth of the large gear
bigTeeth.description: Stage « One very large gear »: how many teeth the large gear has. An event raises it to 120 once the learner has answered, and the gear grows to that size.

minuteColor.title: Minute shaft
minuteColor.description: The minute shaft, its small gear and the minute hand, which turn together.

middleColor.title: Middle gears
middleColor.description: The large gear and the small gear fixed on it, which turn together.

hourColor.title: Hour wheel
hourColor.description: The last gear, its tube and the hour hand, which turn together.

caseColor.title: Case
caseColor.description: The rim of the clock around the dial.

markColor.title: Counted teeth
markColor.description: The teeth that light up as they pass the meeting point.

inkColor.title: Outlines
inkColor.description: The ink of every outline, the dial's ticks and the labels' rims.

hintColor.title: Gesture hints
hintColor.description: The curved arrows that show what can be turned or rolled, until the learner does it.

pause.description: Label of the round button that stops the gears turning.

play.description: Label of the same button once the gears are stopped.

dialLabel.description: Name of the clock for screen readers: arrow keys move the minute hand.

gearsLabel.description: Name of the gears for screen readers: arrow keys turn them.

rollLabel.text: Last gear, to roll back to the centre
rollLabel.description: Name of the last gear before it is back at the centre: arrow keys roll it, Enter takes it all the way.

rollValue.text: {percent}% of the way to the centre
rollValue.description: How far the last gear has rolled towards the centre.

time.description: The time the clock shows, for screen readers. minute has two digits.

turns.text: {n, plural, one {# turn of the small gear} other {# turns of the small gear}}
turns.description: How far the gears have turned, for screen readers.

teethPassed.description: Under the gears: how many teeth of this gear have passed the meeting point.

sizerLabel.description: Name of the slider that sets the number of teeth of the last gear, for screen readers.

slower.description: How much slower the last gear turns than the minute shaft.

xray.description: Switch that makes the dial clear to show the gears behind it.

docked.text: The last gear is on the minute shaft, at the centre.
docked.description: Said to screen readers when the last gear reaches the centre.

matched.text: Twelve times slower: the size of a clock's hour wheel.
matched.description: Said to screen readers when the learner finds the right size.

objects.label: Small gear on the minute shaft

minute.description: Angle of the minute shaft, in radians (negative: clockwise)

w2.description: Teeth chosen for the last gear

orbit.description: Where the last gear stands around its small gear, in radians (π: at the centre)

docked.description: The last gear has reached the centre

matched.description: The learner has sized the last gear for twelve times slower

events.name: train_sized
events.description: The learner lets go of the slider of the last gear.

events.name: train_matched
events.description: The last gear has 32 teeth: the train turns twelve times slower.

events.name: docked
events.description: The last gear has rolled back to the centre, onto the minute shaft.

events.name: gear_grown
events.description: The large gear has grown to the size the learner was asked about.

a11y.description: The gears behind a clock's dial, drawn in flat colours with dark outlines. The minute shaft, its small gear of 10 teeth and the minute hand are coral; a gear of 30 teeth and the gear of 8 fixed on it are yellow; the last gear of 32 teeth, its tube and the hour hand are green. Each screen shows one part of the mechanism: the dial, then two gears, then the whole train.
a11y.keyboard: Tab reaches the gears, then the controls. On the gears, the arrow keys turn them, one tooth at a time (one minute on the dial); in the step where the last gear rolls back to the centre, the arrow keys roll it and Enter takes it there. Space pauses or restarts the motion.
a11y.dragAlternative: Every drag has a keyboard path; a click on the last gear rolls it back to the centre, and the slider sizes it.
